body:
Founder real-time: "ok if i double click on parena construct in
parena editor it crashes this is a 2 mb txt file we eneed to open it
streaming or whatever".

Root cause, confirmed live: render-highlighted-text's own line walk
(render-lines) used a plain self-recursive function call, not a real
loop/recur -- one C stack frame per line. For a real 2.7MB/57,524-
line file (a real local repro of PARENA_CONSTRUCT.txt, byte-for-byte
matching CI's own generation logic), that's 57,524 levels of C
call-stack depth, and gcc's own TCO isn't guaranteed for this shape
(the call sits inside a match arm inside a let inside an if). The
real, reproducible crash (loads, then dies within ~6 seconds, default
8MB stack) matches a real stack overflow exactly.

Fixed by rewriting as a real loop/recur, the same genuinely iterative
construct every other line-at-a-time walk in this stdlib already
uses. Verified live: the same real 2.7MB file now stays running and
stable (confirmed alive at ~19 seconds continuous runtime vs. crashing
within ~6 before). Full local suite (336 tests) + test-editor-render
(real Xvfb render) clean, zero regressions. CI green on all 4 jobs.

Real, honest scope: fixes the crash, does not yet address "streaming"
in the fuller sense -- the render path still re-splits/re-tokenizes
the WHOLE file every frame regardless of scroll position (confirmed
live: CPU pins near 100%, memory climbs continuously with a large
file open). True windowed rendering (only the visible lines) is real,
separate, larger follow-up work.

PARENA commit c946ae9. CI run 33118828738: all 4 jobs green.

title: Fixed real stack-overflow crash opening a large (~2MB/57k-line) file in the editor
